scope.purpose: Design development-only research on one shared three-product menu before running the proposed comparison.
scope.v1_policy: Do not modify V1 frozen source, manifests or saved outcomes.
scope.disclosure: Earlier holdout exposure cannot be reversed. These are exploratory development comparisons and internal validation, not a newly pristine final test.

primary_recommendation.name: Coverage first, then minimize maximum growth regret, with explicit catalogue extension if demand identifies fewer than three products

candidate_weights.execution: One common annual fixed-target rebalancing rule with the task's self-financing transfer cost, including initial allocation.

risk_policy_cases.interpretation: Alpha and bill floors are explicit service-policy cases, not identified client preferences or calibrated withdrawal reserves. The risk_only case is not a complete liquidity suitability solution.

per_customer_metrics.eligible_set: F_j = {w: breach_count <= floor(n*alpha) and bill_weight >= the explicitly selected liquidity-case floor}
per_customer_metrics.strict_exceedance: D > L; do not silently change the event to D >= L.
per_customer_metrics.integer_screen: Implement the count threshold directly. At n=96 and alpha=.10 the maximum allowable count is 9, not 9.6; disclose the resulting empirical resolution.

shared_menu_and_assignment.menu: One set M of at most three distinct weight vectors, shared by all five representative profiles.
shared_menu_and_assignment.assignment: For each client choose the largest g_j among M intersect F_j; if that set is empty, refer to human review.
assignment_ties: Fixed lexicographic weight order for remaining numerical ties
shared_menu_and_assignment.no_hidden_fourth_product: A client-specific feasible optimum may be computed only as a diagnostic regret benchmark. It must never be offered, traded, or used as a fallback outside the shared menu.

menu_objective.benchmark: g_star_j = max_{w in F_j} g_j(w), when F_j is nonempty.
menu_objective.regret: r_j(M) = g_star_j - max_{w in M intersect F_j} g_j(w), only for clients covered by M.
lexicographic_order: Maximize the number of the five representative clients covered by the menu.
Among maximum-coverage menus, minimize the maximum annualized expected-log growth regret over covered clients.
Among those menus, minimize mean regret over covered clients.
menu_objective.empty_coverage: If no representative client is coverable, define regret comparisons as vacuous and identify zero demand-supported products; proceed only with the explicitly labelled reference-frontier catalogue extension.
menu_objective.coverage_set_audit: Retain the identities of covered and referred clients, not only their count. At equal coverage, regret over covered clients can favor a different subset; this is not a guarantee of fairness to every uncovered client.
menu_objective.tie_tolerance_interpretation: Floating-point equality only, not a practical growth-indifference band.
normative_choices: Serving an additional representative client has priority over improving growth for already covered clients.
Worst-client opportunity loss is prioritized before average efficiency.
Annualized log-growth regret is compared in the same units across horizons.
The five supplied profiles receive equal representational standing; they are not an estimated customer-population distribution.

fewer_than_three_demand_supported_produc.required_diagnostic: Compute the optimal objective vector separately for menu cardinalities one, two and three; use zero if nobody is coverable.
fewer_than_three_demand_supported_produc.identified_cardinality: The smallest cardinality attaining the three-product optimum under the numerical tie tolerance.
fewer_than_three_demand_supported_produc.do_not_force_usage: Do not require each product to serve a supplied profile solely to manufacture three labels. This could worsen suitability or make the problem infeasible.
fewer_than_three_demand_supported_produc.reference_horizon_reason: The median of the five stated horizons, used as a descriptive catalogue reference, not a population estimate.
fewer_than_three_demand_supported_produc.reference_tail_level_scope: Fixed CVaR level used for catalogue description across all alpha policy cases; it is not an extra eligibility constraint.
fewer_than_three_demand_supported_produc.frontier: Training-fold Pareto frontier of larger g_15 and smaller CVaR_0.90(MDD_15), retaining nondominated distinct targets.
fewer_than_three_demand_supported_produc.extension_rule: After selecting the minimal demand-supported menu, fill remaining slots from the reference frontier by maximizing the minimum absolute CVaR_0.90 distance to existing products. With an empty menu, start from the minimum-risk frontier endpoint. Repeat until three targets exist.
fewer_than_three_demand_supported_produc.interpretation: An extension slot broadens the risk spectrum of the catalogue. It is not identified by the five customers and must not be claimed to improve their coverage or regret.
fewer_than_three_demand_supported_produc.completion_assertion: The completed menu must retain the computed three-product optimum's coverage and regret vector. An improving completion reveals a selection or tie-handling error; a worsening completion is not admissible.
fewer_than_three_demand_supported_produc.degeneracy: If the union of demand-supported products and available reference-frontier extensions cannot supply three distinct targets or three reference risk levels, report the precise limitation. Demand-supported products need not all lie on the H15 frontier. Do not manufacture risk separation by renaming tied targets.

product_labels.ordering: Sort final targets by increasing training-fold CVaR_0.90(MDD_15); use Conservative, Balanced, Growth only as reference-horizon labels.
product_labels.risk_ties: Retain an explicit tied-risk flag; deterministic weight ordering is not evidence of risk separation.
product_labels.crossing_interpretation: If risk order reverses at another horizon, label the hierarchy reference-horizon-specific. Do not claim global monotone risk ordering.

fixed_comparator.name: Reference-H15 risk representative menu
construction: Construct the training-only g_15 versus CVaR_0.90(MDD_15) Pareto frontier.
Choose the minimum-risk frontier endpoint and the maximum-growth endpoint.
Choose a distinct interior frontier point closest to the midpoint of those endpoints' tail-risk values.
fixed_comparator.normative_choices: H15 is the median reference horizon; the middle product represents half the risk range, not an empirically identified Balanced preference.
fixed_comparator.degeneracy: If fewer than three nondominated distinct risk points exist, report the limitation instead of inventing a third Pareto point.
fixed_comparator.comparison_policy: Evaluate this predeclared comparator; do not retrospectively replace the primary method merely because one cached comparison looks better.

empirical_tail_calculation.var: Use the empirical-CDF generalized inverse, such as quantile(method='inverted_cdf'), when a quantile is intended to correspond to the empirical chance constraint.
empirical_tail_calculation.cvar: For beta=.90 use eta + mean(max(D-eta,0))/(1-beta), minimized in eta; an empirical generalized-inverse beta-quantile is a valid minimizer.
empirical_tail_calculation.fractional_tail: At n=96 the worst 10% has mass 9.6 observations. Do not simply average the worst 10 observations without fractional weighting.
empirical_tail_calculation.reported_p90: If linear-interpolated P90 is also reported, distinguish that descriptive statistic from the generalized-inverse VaR used mathematically.

internal_validation.split_rule: Seeded permutation of the 120 scenario IDs into five fixed groups; keep every complete scenario in one group.
internal_validation.training_boundary: For every fold and every policy case, fit the metric summaries, reference frontier, demand menu, extension products and customer assignments from scratch using only its 96 training scenarios.
internal_validation.test_boundary: Freeze the shared menu and each customer's selected product or referral before evaluating the 24 test paths. Do not inspect held-out losses to switch to another product or the oracle.
internal_validation.referrals: Retain referrals in the coverage denominator. Do not impute their investment returns as zero or silently give them a bill-only fourth product.
internal_validation.pooled_oof: The pooled out-of-fold results describe the 96-scenario learning procedure with different fold-trained menus, not performance of one fixed final 120-scenario menu.
internal_validation.uncertainty_scope: Training folds overlap, so pooled out-of-fold outcomes do not justify a naive independent-binomial certification of the selected learning procedure.

resolution_check.scope: Only the union of simplex neighborhoods within one coarse swap, L1 distance <=.10, of the originally selected coarse-grid products.
resolution_check.purpose: Check coverage, screen boundaries, menu regret and target sensitivity to discretization; do not replace the declared coarse-grid primary result in pursuit of better growth.

complete_reselection_bootstrap.unit: Whole scenario IDs, retaining all years, assets and inflation jointly.
complete_reselection_bootstrap.procedure: Resample 120 whole scenarios with replacement; recompute all candidate metrics and rerun the complete menu selection and assignment, including minimal-cardinality and catalogue-extension rules.
complete_reselection_bootstrap.alignment: For weight-distribution diagnostics align products by minimum total L1 distance to the reference menu over all six permutations; also retain each replicate's H15 risk-order labels.
required_outputs: Automatic versus referral frequency per client
Reference risk-order and cross-horizon crossing frequencies
complete_reselection_bootstrap.precision_note: With 200 replicates, a reported frequency near one half has Monte Carlo standard error about 3.5 percentage points. Replicate count is a computational precision choice, not extra market evidence.
complete_reselection_bootstrap.optional_oob: If selected products are scored on out-of-bag paths, report their varying sample sizes and call the results diagnostics; repeated out-of-bag evaluations overlap and do not create independent tail samples.
complete_reselection_bootstrap.nested_cv_caution: If bootstrapping cross-validation, all duplicate copies of an original scenario must remain in its same original fold; never allow duplicate paths in both training and test.
complete_reselection_bootstrap.prohibited_claim: No pointwise Clopper-Pearson or Wilson upper bound calculated after menu selection on the same sample is a certificate for the selected menu. Reselection bootstrap distributions are not such a certificate either.

executable_diagnostic_grades.separate_axes: Do not collapse normative policy dependence, sampling sensitivity, numerical sensitivity and parameter identifiability into one supposed probability of safety.

empirical_screen.one_scenario_boundary_pass: k == floor(n*alpha): changing one non-breach path to a breach can reverse the screen.
empirical_screen.one_scenario_boundary_fail: k == floor(n*alpha)+1: changing one breach path to a non-breach can reverse the screen.

policy_dependence.P0: Coverage and assigned reference role are unchanged across the declared policy cases.
policy_dependence.P1: Product or role changes across policy cases, but auto/referral status does not.
policy_dependence.P2: Auto/referral status changes with alpha or the declared liquidity floor.
policy_dependence.meaning: These are normative policy effects, not necessarily sampling failure. Report both fixed-base-menu counterfactual screening and full menu reselection if feasible, since they answer different questions.

sampling_sensitivity.consistent_referral: The full-development fit and all five training folds refer the client; no automatic suitability claim is supported.
sampling_sensitivity.development_consistent_auto: Full-development assignment passes its empirical screen, all five training folds provide an eligible automatic product, pooled OOF empirical exceedance is <=alpha, and the full-development screen is not one-scenario-boundary-pass.
sampling_sensitivity.sampling_sensitive: At least one training fold refers while another provides an automatic product, or the full-development screen is one-scenario-boundary-pass.
sampling_sensitivity.internal_calibration_warning: For clients with frozen fold-level automatic assignments, their pooled OOF empirical exceedance rate exceeds alpha; retain the actual counts and denominators and do not reinterpret this as proof about the population probability.
sampling_sensitivity.bootstrap_role: Report the continuous reselection frequencies and functional outcome distributions alongside these flags. Do not choose an unannounced bootstrap approval cutoff after seeing its values.
sampling_sensitivity.not_certification: Development-consistent means no specified internal warning was observed; it is not a guarantee, a formal population-probability confidence statement, or independent final validation.

numerical_sensitivity.flag: The local 2.5% resolution check changes coverage or any client's auto/referral status, or changes whether the three reference risks are distinct.
numerical_sensitivity.otherwise: Report the actual functional and weight changes; absence of this flag is not proof of grid independence.

executable_diagnostic_grades.parameter_vs_function: Large weight variability with nearly unchanged coverage, growth regret and risk diagnostics is parameter non-identifiability on a flat objective, not necessarily functional instability. Keep these conclusions separate.

mandatory_claim_boundaries: This method defines a three-target menu, not five customer-specific portfolios.
Three supplied product names do not imply that all three must be chosen by the five supplied profiles.
A risk-spectrum extension is an explicit catalogue policy, not estimated customer demand.
Expected excess loss is a mandatory severity diagnostic, not a hidden severity constraint.
Reference-horizon risk labels do not guarantee ordering at every customer horizon.
Coverage over five representative profiles is not customer-population coverage.
Synthetic empirical risk budgets and internal development consistency do not certify real-world loss probabilities.
